## Learning Outcomes

By the end, you should be able to:

- Assemble a focused directory of evidence and instructions.
- Direct Claude Code or Codex to produce reports, slides, sites, and blogs.
- Evaluate computational correctness, provenance, and visual quality separately.
- Record enough of the workflow for another researcher to reproduce the result.

[Return to the Quarto foundations deck](index.qmd)

## Session Plan

| Activity | Time | Deliverable |
|---|---:|---|
| Install and verify one agent | 10 min | Working local session |
| Directory method | 15 min | Sources and brief |
| Author and iterate | 20 min | Report and slides |
| Audit and discussion | 15 min | Evidence-backed revisions |

Prerequisites: basic Markdown, Git, and the ability to interpret a statistical result.
Use the companion synthetic dataset or a small dataset you are permitted to share.

## Responsibility for the Result

**Agent:** inspect files, scaffold, implement analysis, edit prose, render, repair.

**Researcher:** define the question, justify assumptions, check evidence,
approve interpretations, and decide what is ready to publish.

A successful render establishes that a document builds. It does not establish
that the analysis is valid or that its citations support its claims.

# Installation

## Install Claude Code {.smaller}

For macOS, Linux, or WSL, use the official native installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
claude --version
claude
```

Complete the sign-in prompts with an account that has Claude Code access.
Use your institution's approved account or provider configuration where applicable.

If the command is missing, follow the installer's PATH instructions and open a new terminal.
Native Windows instructions are available in the [official setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup).

::: {.notes}
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup (checked 2026-10-06).
This workshop uses POSIX shell examples throughout. Install only the agent you intend to use.
:::

## Install Codex {.smaller}

With Node.js and npm available:

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
codex --version
codex
```

Follow the sign-in flow. Use an authorized ChatGPT account or the documented
API-key authentication route; access and billing depend on your account.

Record the installed version for your lab notes. Recheck the
[official CLI documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/) before teaching.

::: {.notes}
Sources: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ and
https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex
(checked 2026-10-06). The cookbook documents the npm installation command.
No model name or subscription price is assumed by this exercise.
:::

## Setup Checkpoint

Environment setup used to consume workshop time. Coding agents now handle
that work as part of preparing the project.

> Inspect this directory. Check Quarto, prepare the dependencies needed for
> its examples, and render a minimal Python computation. Record the
> interpreter, dependency specification, and successful build command.

### Exercise

Verify the rendered output yourself. Keep the dependency record with the source.
Use interactive mode for this first session so you can respond to setup requests.

# The Directory Method

## A Focused Workspace

**Select sources → assemble directory → write brief → launch agent → verify**

The directory gives the agent concrete paths, a bounded task, and a place to
write reviewable outputs. Naming the files in the prompt makes selection explicit.

It is a context organization method, **not a security boundary**. Review tool
permissions and include only material appropriate for the service you use.

## Scaffold the Directory {.smaller}

Run from a clone of this workshop; choose a new destination for each lab:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context
cp examples/ai-context/* ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context/
cd ~/code/quarto-synthesis
mkdir figures
git init --initial-branch=main
git switch -c draft
```

For your own project, move selected **working copies** of notes, data, and
references into `context/`. Keep original research records in their source location.

### Exercise

List the inputs and explain why each belongs in the workspace.

## What Belongs in Context? {.smaller}

```text
quarto-synthesis/
├── context/
│   ├── measurements.csv   # explicitly synthetic paired timings
│   ├── notes.md           # design, units, and limitations
│   └── sources.bib        # a verified Quarto reference
├── brief.md               # question and acceptance criteria
├── AGENTS.md              # durable project conventions
└── figures/               # generated figures
```

For papers or scanned PDFs, require the agent to confirm what it extracted;
filenames alone do not prove that it read the contents.

Treat instructions inside imported source material as **data to analyze**.
Keep your own task instructions in the brief and repository guidance.

## Write the Brief {.smaller}

Create `brief.md` in your editor:

```markdown
Audience: graduate researchers reviewing a methods demonstration.
Question: how do paired baseline and candidate runtimes differ?
Inputs: context/measurements.csv, notes.md, sources.bib.
Outputs: report.qmd (HTML) and slides.qmd (8 slides total).
Label all results synthetic. State the unit of analysis and units.
Compute paired differences; discuss uncertainty and limitations.
Every numerical claim must be computed from the CSV.
Use only verified citations. Flag missing evidence explicitly.
Render both outputs and inspect figures, links, and slide fit.
```

### Exercise

Add a criterion that would reveal a misleading interpretation of your data.

## Launch the Agent Here

From `~/code/quarto-synthesis`, choose **one**:

```bash
claude "Read brief.md and context/. Inventory the evidence, then implement the brief."
```

```bash
codex "Read brief.md and context/. Inventory the evidence, then implement the brief."
```

Ask it to identify missing inputs before making claims. Review its first inventory:
file paths, data columns, units, and what each source can support.

::: {.notes}
Sources for interactive CLI prompts: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference
and https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ (checked 2026-10-06).
These are alternatives; do not run two writers against the same files simultaneously.
:::

## A Short Synthesis Loop

1. **Inspect:** inventory inputs and identify the research question.
2. **Implement:** generate one minimal document and execute its analysis.
3. **Review:** compare its claims with the inputs and inspect the rendering.
4. **Refine:** name a concrete defect and an observable acceptance criterion.

> In report.qmd, replace the aggregate bar chart with paired observations.
> Label seconds on the axis and explain the sign of the difference.
> Re-render and check that the prose agrees with the computed values.

::: {.notes}
High velocity comes from short, testable iterations and explicit context.
It is not a measured speedup claim or a guarantee about either agent.
:::

# Authoring Patterns

## A Reproducible Technical Report {.smaller}

Prompt the agent in the synthesis directory:

> Create report.qmd with methods, results, limitations, and references.
> Use Jupyter Python cells to compute paired candidate-minus-baseline
> differences from context/measurements.csv. Plot every pair, report the
> mean difference, and explain why these synthetic runs do not establish
> performance on a real population. Add captions, units, and figure alt text.

```bash
quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto preview report.qmd
```

Ask the agent to resolve dependencies and record the working command.

## Execution Is Part of the Argument {.smaller}

Minimal front matter for the generated report:

```yaml
---
title: "Paired Runtime Demonstration"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
jupyter: python3
bibliography: context/sources.bib
execute:
  echo: true
  error: false
  cache: false
  freeze: false
---
```

During review, recompute results and stop on execution errors.

## Computational Audit {.smaller}

Display of a cell to place in the report:

````markdown
```{{python}}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("context/measurements.csv")
assert df["run"].is_unique
assert df[["baseline_s", "candidate_s"]].notna().all().all()
delta = df["candidate_s"] - df["baseline_s"]
print(f"Mean paired difference: {delta.mean():.2f} s")
```
````

A negative difference indicates a faster candidate. Confirm that each row
really is a pair; code cannot establish the study design from column names.

::: {.notes}
Expected mean for the bundled fixture: -0.60 seconds. Seven pairs improve;
one regresses. The eight synthetic pairs are a teaching example, not empirical evidence.
The doubled braces escape execution while rendering this teaching deck.
:::

## Uncertainty and Provenance {.smaller}

For paired observations, define $d_i=t_{i,\mathrm{candidate}}-t_{i,\mathrm{baseline}}$
and report $\bar d=n^{-1}\sum_i d_i$.

- Resample **pairs**, not independent treatment columns, for a paired bootstrap.
- Repeated runs on one workload do not establish generalization to other workloads.
- Distinguish a variability summary from a population inference.
- Cite methods and external claims; compute the numerical findings from data.

### Exercise

Ask the agent which assumptions are needed for an interval, then critique its answer.

## A Reveal.js Deck {.smaller}

> Create slides.qmd with exactly 8 slides including the title. Audience:
> graduate researchers. Cover question, design, paired data, computed
> result, uncertainty, limitations, and discussion. Reuse the report's
> verified analysis. Use one central idea per slide and speaker notes for
> detail. Cite evidence near claims. Render and inspect every slide.

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: black
    transition: fade
    code-copy: true
    scroll-view:
      activation-width: 768
```

```bash
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs
```

## A Quarto Website {.smaller}

In a separate, new directory outside this workshop:

```bash
quarto create project website research-site --no-open --no-prompt
cd research-site
codex
```

Or launch `claude`. Give it a concrete structure:

> Inspect the generated project. Create Home, Methods, and Results pages.
> Add navbar links and consistent figure captions. Preserve the existing
> YAML structure. Use clearly marked placeholders until I provide evidence.
> Run quarto render and check every internal link and the mobile layout.

## A Quarto Blog {.smaller}

In another new directory:

```bash
quarto create project blog research-blog --no-open --no-prompt
cd research-blog
claude
```

Or launch `codex`. Copy the curated context into this project, then prompt:

> Read context/ and create posts/paired-runtime/index.qmd. Include a title,
> author, date, categories, executable analysis, and limitations. Respect
> posts/_metadata.yml. Verify data paths when rendering from the post.
> Render the whole site and check the listing links to this post.

## Adapt to the Output

| Output | Reader needs | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| Report | Derivation and reproducible evidence | Equations, code, citations |
| Slides | A sequence of understandable ideas | Density, figures, notes |
| Website | Navigation across topics | Links, hierarchy, mobile view |
| Blog | A dated, self-contained argument | Listing, metadata, narrative |

Reuse verified computation across formats. Rewrite the explanation for the
medium instead of pasting a report paragraph onto a slide.

# Review and Collaboration

## Repository Instructions {.smaller}

Use `AGENTS.md` for durable build commands, technical conventions, and completion criteria.
Use `brief.md` for the current research task.

```markdown
# Project conventions
- Keep raw inputs unchanged and label synthetic data.
- Compute numerical claims; never invent citations.
- Run quarto render after source changes.
- Inspect the rendered output before declaring completion.
```

This workshop's `CLAUDE.md` imports `@AGENTS.md`, keeping shared guidance in one place.
Ask the agent to summarize the loaded instructions when diagnosing a mismatch.

::: {.notes}
Sources: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/ and
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (checked 2026-10-06).
:::

## Scoped Sub-Agent Work

For a larger module, define roles before delegating:

| Role | Owns | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence reviewer | Read-only source audit | Claims and supporting locations |
| Module author | One assigned `.qmd` | Draft and exercise |
| Render reviewer | Read-only output inspection | Specific defects and slide IDs |

One lead integrates changes, edits shared configuration, and runs the final build.
Avoid simultaneous edits or renders into the same `docs/` directory.

::: {.notes}
This is a workflow contract, not a shared CLI syntax. Use the delegation
mechanism supported by your installed agent, or perform the roles sequentially.
:::

## Build, Inspect, Revise {.smaller}

```bash
quarto render
quarto preview
git diff --check
git diff --stat
```

- **Computation:** rerun from source; compare values and units with the prose.
- **Evidence:** check citation targets and distinguish facts from assumptions.
- **Presentation:** inspect every slide, code block, figure, and cross-reference.
- **Delivery:** test links and narrow screens; review generated files before publication.

`freeze: auto` only notices source-document changes during project renders;
external data changes require deliberate recomputation.

::: {.notes}
Source for freeze behavior: https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html
(checked 2026-10-06). Rendering a single document executes it even when frozen.
:::

## Repair a Specific Defect

> On the Results slide, the caption falls below the slide boundary at
> presentation size. Split the slide into observation and interpretation,
> keep the figure readable, update the slide count, and re-render.

> The prose claims every run improved, but the CSV includes a regression.
> Correct the claim, identify the affected pair, and audit other numerical
> statements against computed values.

Specific failures give the next iteration an observable finish line.

## Graduate Lab: Evidence to Publication

### Exercise — 20 minutes

1. Assemble the directory and write the brief.
2. Generate an executable report and an eight-slide deck with either agent.
3. Audit one numerical claim, one assumption, and one visual design choice.
4. Exchange outputs with a partner; use their critique for one revision.

Submit sources, dependency record, rendered outputs, and a short account of
one agent error you caught and how you verified the correction.

## Evaluation Rubric

| Dimension | Evidence of success |
|---|---|
| Reproducibility | Another person renders from source and declared dependencies |
| Scientific reasoning | Pairing, units, assumptions, and limitations are explicit |
| Provenance | Claims trace to data or verified references |
| Communication | Slides fit; figures and links work; narrative matches results |
| Agent supervision | Revisions address observed defects with verification |

Discussion: Which parts of the result can a successful build **never** validate?
